According to [The Mixtape](https://mixtape.scunning.com/09-difference_in_differences#potential-outcomes-and-identification), "diff-in-diff is a causal design, not simply four numbers subtracted in a row."

"Design" implies some assignment to treatment by the researcher, otherwise it's "simply four numbers subtracted in a row" plus "assume a can opener" (parallel trends).
To get parallel trends by design probably means some kind of random assignment.
But then you probably don't want to do diff-in-diff:

[Evaluating natural experiments](https://iangow.github.io/far_book/natural-revisited.html#evaluating-natural-experiments), in *Empirical Research in Accounting: Tools and Methods*.
